cues.text: Hello Sam, come in and sit down ...
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Thanks.
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: You’re here to discuss your company-based IT project aren’t you?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Yes ... I’ve been to see the Manager and he’s given me a lot of ideas about projects that the company would find useful. But I wanted to ask your opinion about them before I choose one.
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: Yes, that’s fine. Now this company’s called Turners isn’t it?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: That’s right. It’s a small engineering company - they make machine components for trade use. They’re well established - they started in nineteen seventy-six - but they’re a bit old fashioned.
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: OK ... And what kind of projects did Turners suggest you could do for the company?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Well, they want some improvements made to their customer database. The one that they’ve got at the moment isn’t very useful in some ways. I had a quick look at it ...
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: That would be a very straightforward project, and it’d be simple enough to evaluate, but I don’t think you’d get enough out of a project like that. You wouldn’t learn anything new.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Well another project they suggested is to do with their online sales catalogue. At the moment customers can look at their products but they can’t actually order them online, which must affect their competitiveness. But I said I thought it would take too long, it’s quite a big task.
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: You’re right. It’s too much for the time you’ve got. It’s a pity though.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Then they want some help with their payroll system. At the moment the way they calculate pay involves a lot of manual accounting. I suggested they could have a system where employees register electronically when they arrive and leave work, so the hours they do could be transferred automatically.
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: I think you’d get a lot out of a project like that - it would extend your skills but it wouldn’t be too much to take on. A student did something similar a couple of years ago, but this is slightly different.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Well, then they need help with their stock inventory. They do everything manually ...
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: Really?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Yes! And it takes so much time.
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: It’s probably very inaccurate too ... An electronic inventory would probably be the biggest single benefit for the company. I’m surprised they haven’t had it done before.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I know! Then they wanted to improve their internal security. The Manager had visited other companies where the staff use swipe cards to access various areas of the building ... It sounded useful, but the trouble is, I’m not really sure how to do it.
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: Well, I think you’re right in that assessment. At the moment it’s probably a bit beyond your level of knowledge. Is that all?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Just one more ... Customer Service. They want to be able to collect feedback from their customers in a more systematic way. At the moment it’s a bit of a mess, and they probably lose business as a result.
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: Would that involve you going to see customers at their own premises? Because in that case you might have to do a fair amount of travelling, and that would incur expenses that haven’t been agreed with these companies.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I never thought of that ...
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: Well it might not be a problem, but it’s something that needs clarifying ... Well I hope that’s been helpful in narrowing down the options?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Yes it has, thanks. I’ll be able to make a decision now. But while I’m here, can I talk to you about coursework?
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: Sure .
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I’m not very happy about the way our group assignment is working. There are some problems .
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: Oh dear. Are people just not getting on with each other? That’s the worst thing ...
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Actually we’re all friends, it’s not that, but when we’re having a discussion about the assignment one or two people end up doing all the talking, and the rest don’t say anything. It’s a bit frustrating, because we need plenty of debate ...
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: Well that’s a common observation. You’re studying in a group with people from all over the world, and you all have your own ways of participating. In some places students are more used to listening than talking, and vice versa.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Mmm. I suppose you’re right ... I’ll try to remember that ...
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: Does everyone pull their weight as far as sharing the workload is concerned?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I’d say they do, yes. And our group elected a leader. She’s very good at making sure no one’s overloaded ... But personally I feel that there are just too many of us in the group. Whenever we try to arrange a meeting there’s always at least one person who can’t make it. It’s not anyone’s fault. It’s just that we’ve all got slightly different timetables.
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: Well I’m glad you’ve talked to me about it. Feedback is always useful. Is there anything else you’re concerned about?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: There are a couple of problems with lecturers that all the students are talking about ...
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: Last semester we had negative feedback about the way lectures were organised. There were several occasions when the wrong room had been booked, or the same room had been booked twice ... that sort of thing. Is that still a problem?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: That hasn’t happened at all as far as I know ...
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: Oh good, it’s sorted out then.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: But ... I don’t know the reason, but some of the staff often turn up late, so we miss ten or fifteen minutes of our lecture time ... It might be because they’ve been copying handouts for students, I think there’s a queue for the machine sometimes ...
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: Well I’ll look into that. Thank you for telling me. Anything else?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: The other thing is that it can be very difficult to get to see a lecturer individually. They’re all very supportive and friendly when you do manage to find them, but often they’re not in their office, even at times when they’re meant to be available for consultation.
cues.speaker: Sam

cues.text: OK ... That’s helpful ... Now before you leave, let me...
cues.speaker: Tutor
